q: Is the pWR100 virulence-plasmid IcsA/IpaBCD T3SS effector repertoire complete and stable across in-vitro and in-vivo passages of S. flexneri 5a M90T, or does the deposited GCF_004799585.1 pWR100 (232,195 bp) capture only a snapshot subject to effector loss/duplication drift?
basis: The replication reconstructed the full T3SS repertoire on pWR100 via VFDB/Victors (mxi/spa apparatus, ipa invasins + ipg chaperones, osp + ipaH effectors, virF/virB regulators, icsA/virG motility) at a single time point from the paper's deposit. Cervantes-Rivera 2020 reports a complete gapless pWR100 from a specific M90T lineage passage at Umea/MIMS; multiple prior pWR501 (AF348706) and pINV sequences have shown effector-repertoire variability, and IS-mediated deletion of individual osp/ipaH loci is documented in Shigella pINV curing literature. Whether the 2020 M90T pWR100 effector list is genotypically stable across labs and passages is not tested here.
next_steps: Long-read (PacBio HiFi or ONT R10) re-sequence pWR100 from >=3 independent M90T sublines (Sansonetti frozen stock, MIMS current stock, another benchmark lab) at early and late passage; assemble each with Flye/Canu; compare effector-locus presence/absence and IS-boundary coordinates; catalog gain/loss events per passage. Cross-reference against the 232,195 bp CP037924.1 reference and quantify effector-repertoire stability rate.

q: How much of the S. flexneri M90T chromosome's 'hybrid E. coli-Shigella' pathoadaptive evolution signal is genuine ancestral signal versus reference-quality assembly gaps concentrated in IS-rich and repeat-rich regions, given the 402 IS elements and 769 pseudogenes in a 4,596,714 bp chromosome?
basis: The paper reports 402 IS elements and 769 pseudogenes on the chromosome (296 chrom + 106 plasmid IS; 640 chrom + 129 plasmid pseudo) as evidence of Shigella reductive evolution from an E. coli ancestor. This replication corroborated pseudogene load (Prokka+RefSeq PGAP within ~1.5%) but explicitly did NOT re-type IS elements independently (ISfinder/ISEScan not run) and observed a large ~18% CDS-count delta between PGAP (4,053) and paper Prokka+curation (4,949). IS-rich and low-complexity regions are the exact loci where PacBio-only assemblies with ~157x coverage can mis-collapse tandem repeats or over-split near IS boundaries, potentially inflating apparent pseudogenization.
next_steps: Run ISEScan and ISfinder independently on CP037923.1 to reproduce the 402 IS count and locate every IS-family member; overlay against pseudogene annotations to compute IS-adjacent pseudogene rate. Cross-map to a fully-assembled E. coli K-12 reference to distinguish Shigella-specific pseudogenization from shared-ancestor pseudogenes. If ONT R10+ or PacBio HiFi (Q30+) re-sequencing of M90T becomes available, re-assemble and check for structural variants in IS-rich contigs that would revise the reductive-evolution numbers.

q: How conserved is the serotype-2a rfb (LPS O-antigen) biosynthesis cluster compared to the serotype-5a M90T rfb cluster on the CP037923.1 chromosome, and which O-antigen glycosyltransferases and Wzy/Wzx components represent cross-serotype conserved vaccine antigens?
basis: M90T is the serotype-5a reference strain (this paper's subject; Cervantes-Rivera 2020), but epidemiologically dominant Shigella flexneri outbreak lineages are serotype 2a. Cross-serotype LPS conservation is the pivotal design question for broadly-protective S. flexneri glycoconjugate vaccines. This replication established the complete 4,596,714 bp M90T chromosome CP037923.1 as an independently-verified reference but did not annotate or extract the rfb cluster, nor compare it across serotypes.
next_steps: Extract the rfb/rfc/rfa/gtr region from CP037923.1 by homology to the published S. flexneri 2a str. 301 (BA000018) and 2457T (AE014073) rfb clusters using blastn/mummer; align Wzy polymerase, Wzx flippase, and serotype-specific glycosyltransferases (gtrI/II/V/X/A/B/C); compute per-gene identity and coverage. Cross-reference against WHO-listed candidate O-antigen vaccine components (e.g., GVGH/Sanofi flexyn2a, LPS-CRM197) to score which glycan-biosynthesis genes are >=95% identical between 5a M90T and 2a outbreak isolates and thus viable pan-serotype antigen targets.

q: What is the empirical spontaneous plasmid-loss (pINV curing) rate for the 232,195 bp pWR100 mxi-spa T3SS operon under standard in-vitro Congo-Red-agar and LB passage conditions with M90T, and how fast does virulence attenuate as a function of passage number?
basis: The paper establishes pWR100 as the essential T3SS-carrying virulence megaplasmid (independently reproduced here: mxiA-N + spa9-47 structural apparatus, ipa invasins, osp/ipaH effectors, virF/virB regulators all mapped to CP037924.1). Congo-Red-agar colony color loss (white = pINV-cured) is the classical M90T laboratory phenotypic screen for plasmid curing, but the quantitative loss rate per generation and its correlation with graded T3SS attenuation (partial loss of specific effector cassettes vs. total plasmid loss) is not tested by this replication and is not settled in the primary literature for the specific 2020 M90T lineage.
next_steps: Passage M90T (this exact GCF_004799585.1 lineage, MIMS provenance) in LB without Congo-Red selection over 200+ generations; sample every 20 generations; plate on Congo-Red agar and count white (cured) vs. red (pINV+) colonies to estimate loss rate per generation. Long-read sequence >=10 white colonies to check for whole-plasmid loss vs. deletion of specific mxi/spa/ipa cassettes. Correlate loss rate with a HeLa-cell invasion assay and Sereny test (guinea pig keratoconjunctivitis) to build attenuation-kinetics curves.

q: What structural variants (chromosomal inversions, IS-mediated deletions, prophage insertions, plasmid recombination events) distinguish the reference S. flexneri 5a M90T CP037923.1/CP037924.1 assembly from contemporary clinical serotype-2a outbreak isolates (e.g., MSM-associated European clonal lineages, South Asian endemic strains), and are any of these SVs associated with clinical severity, antimicrobial resistance carriage, or transmissibility?
basis: This replication independently verified the complete-genome reference for the laboratory strain M90T (2 circular replicons: 4,596,714 + 232,195 bp), including MLST ST631 and the intrinsic-only AMR profile (blaEC ampC + emrE efflux, NO acquired resistance), confirming M90T's laboratory-reference identity. Clinical outbreak isolates of Shigella flexneri (esp. serotype 2a) increasingly carry ESBL/carbapenemase plasmids, are dominated by different sequence types, and are known to exhibit SVs, prophage variation, and IS-driven rearrangements relative to M90T. The M90T reference itself does NOT capture this clinical variation, and comparative-SV analysis was out of scope for this replication.
next_steps: Pull long-read (PacBio HiFi / ONT R10) assemblies of >=20 recent clinical S. flexneri 2a isolates from public archives (PathogenWatch, EnteroBase, NCBI SRA); align each to CP037923.1 chromosome with mummer/minimap2; call structural variants with syri/nucdiff; catalog inversions, IS-mediated deletions, and prophage insertions. Overlay AMR carriage (AMRFinderPlus, ResFinder), ST, and epidemiological metadata (outbreak, geography, MSM transmission cluster) to test whether specific SVs (e.g., recombination in rfb, ompA, ompC) co-segregate with clinical severity, ESBL plasmid carriage, or transmission fitness.
